## 1. Exact pricing table (USD per 1M tokens)

DeepSeek's pricing page distinguishes input cache hits from input cache misses. As of 2026-04-27, **cache-hit prices were reduced to 1/10 of their prior values** in a system-wide change [thenextweb]. The Next Web confirms the cache-hit reduction was effective immediately. **Note: the 1/10 figure refers to the change relative to prior cache-hit prices, not to the cache-miss price.** The actual cache-hit-to-cache-miss ratio is 1:120 for V4-Pro ($0.0145/$1.74) and 1:50 for V4-Flash ($0.0028/$0.14) — both substantially below 1:10.

| Model | Input cache hit | Input cache miss | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4-pro` (standard, post-promo) | $0.0145 | $1.74 | $3.48 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` (PROMO, 75% off until 2026-05-05 15:59 UTC) | $0.003625 | $0.435 | $0.87 |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` (no promo) | $0.0028 | $0.14 | $0.28 |

Direct quote from the pricing page: *"PROMOTIONAL pricing (limited-time 75% discount on deepseek-v4-pro until 2026-05-05 15:59 UTC) ... REGULAR pricing for deepseek-v4-pro (post-2026-05-05): Input cache hit: $0.0145, Input cache miss: $1.74, Output: $3.48"* [api-docs-pricing]. The page also states: *"The expense = number of tokens × price"* [api-docs-pricing].

Context window is 1M tokens for both models with 384K maximum output [api-docs-pricing]. OpenRouter mirrors V4-Pro at the promotional $0.435 / $0.87 rate and V4-Flash at $0.14 / $0.28, advertising a `1,048,576` token context window [openrouter-v4-pro, openrouter-v4-flash].

**Caveat on TNW figures:** The Next Web article cites V4-Pro standard input as $0.145, which conflates cache-hit pricing with cache-miss pricing — the official DeepSeek page lists $0.0145 cache-hit and $1.74 cache-miss [thenextweb vs api-docs-pricing]. Where the two disagree, the official page is authoritative.

## 2. Comparison to competitor frontier

**V4-Pro at standard pricing.** Simon Willison frames V4-Pro at $1.74 / $3.48 as *"beats all larger frontier models on cost"*, benchmarks trailing state-of-the-art by approximately 3-6 months [simon-willison]. MIT Technology Review confirms the same rates and writes that V4-Pro *"competes with leading closed-source models, matching the performance of Anthropic's Claude-Opus-4.6, OpenAI's GPT-5.4, and Google's Gemini-3.1"* [mit-tech-review]. The Next Web states V4-Pro at standard *"undercuts GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.7"* [thenextweb]. The user prompt's ~1/6-of-Opus-4.7 and ~1/9-of-GPT-5.5 ratios are consistent with TNW's framing but not directly stated — treat as derivable, not quoted.

**V4-Flash.** TNW: Flash *"undercuts GPT-5.4 Nano, Gemini 3.1 Flash, GPT-5.4 Mini, Claude Haiku 4.5"* [thenextweb]. Willison gives the comparison point: *"V4-Flash undercuts OpenAI's GPT-5.4 Nano ($0.20/$1.25)"* [simon-willison] — roughly 30% cheaper on input and ~4.5× cheaper on output.

## 6. Deprecation

The DeepSeek April 24, 2026 release notes state: *"deepseek-chat & deepseek-reasoner will be fully retired and inaccessible after Jul 24th, 2026, 15:59 (UTC Time)"* [api-docs-news260424]. The pricing page clarifies the routing: *"deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner are deprecated aliases — they correspond to the non-thinking and thinking modes of deepseek-v4-flash, respectively"* [api-docs-pricing]. Migration is mechanical: *"Keep base_url, just update model"* [api-docs-news260424], and both V4 models support OpenAI ChatCompletions and Anthropic API shapes [api-docs-news260424].

Net effect: any client still calling `deepseek-chat` or `deepseek-reasoner` past 2026-07-24 15:59 UTC will hard-fail; routing already lands on V4-Flash today.

## 7. Reliability history

**January 2025 — Wiz Research disclosure (15+ months before V4 release).** Wiz found a publicly accessible ClickHouse database at `oauth2callback.deepseek.com:8123/9000` and `dev.deepseek.com:8123/9000` with **zero authentication**, exposing *"chat history, secret keys, backend details, and other highly sensitive information"* across more than 1 million log entries [wiz-database-leak]. Wiz disclosed responsibly and *"DeepSeek promptly secured the exposure"* [wiz-database-leak]. Wiz's own framing notes: *"the structural security posture demonstrated has not been publicly remediated by an audit"* [wiz-database-leak]. No comparable confirmed breach has surfaced for late 2025 or 2026 in this batch.

**March 30, 2026 — outage.** Bloomberg's article on a seven-hour DeepSeek outage was inaccessible (HTTP 403 paywall) [bloomberg-outage]. Substitute citations from the same fetch note: StatusGator tracked **13 incidents in 90 days** through April 2026 (6 major, 7 minor); a Chinese-language source on `eu.36kr.com` reported a 13-hour outage trending on social media; WebProNews described a separate "12-hour outage [that] exposed fragility" with 74+ outages tracked over roughly a year [bloomberg-outage]. **The seven-hour duration and Bloomberg's specific framing are not directly verifiable from a primary source in this batch — flag as paywall-blocked.**
